details:
TerraSpace Analog Explorer

TerraSpace Analog Explorer is an interactive web application designed to explore Earth environments that may serve as analogues for future human exploration and research on the Moon and Mars.

The project helps users investigate and compare different Earth locations using environmental information such as temperature, humidity, precipitation, and solar radiation. It brings environmental data and geographical information together in one platform, helping users explore how different regions on Earth compare in their environmental characteristics.

The application identifies and organizes 192 candidate Earth locations and presents their geographical information, including latitude, longitude, and distance. Users can explore environmental groupings, select date ranges, examine available environmental records, and compare locations through interactive visualizations. The platform also provides information about its methodology and data sources to help users understand how the comparisons are made.

Benefits and intended impact:
TerraSpace makes environmental and geographical information easier to explore and understand through an accessible, interactive platform. It can support students, educators, researchers, and space enthusiasts in studying Earth environments that may be useful for planetary analogue research. By bringing multiple environmental indicators together, the project encourages data-informed exploration and provides a foundation for future research into potential Moon and Mars analogue environments.

Tools and technologies:
The project was developed using Python as the main programming language, Streamlit for the interactive web application, and Pandas for handling and organizing environmental datasets. NASA POWER data is used to obtain environmental information. The application is deployed as a web-based platform, allowing users to access it through a browser.

Creativity and innovation:
The creative aspect of TerraSpace is the integration of geographical exploration, environmental data, date-based analysis, and interactive comparisons in a single platform. Instead of presenting isolated datasets, it gives users an opportunity to explore multiple candidate locations and understand their environmental characteristics together. The project also establishes a foundation for a future feature called **MissionTwin**, which aims to support more advanced matching between Earth environments and selected lunar or Martian conditions.

Factors considered:
Our team considered the relevance of environmental conditions to planetary analogue research, the availability of accessible scientific data, geographical coverage, the ability to compare multiple locations, usability, and transparency of the methodology. We also considered the importance of distinguishing descriptive environmental comparisons from confirmed conclusions about the suitability of a location for an actual space mission.

TerraSpace Analog Explorer aims to make Earth analogue exploration more accessible today while creating a foundation for more advanced planetary research in the future.
